contract.nasaPowerHourlyPayloadValidation: Every location must report UTC, Celsius T2M, reviewed coordinates at NASA response precision, and all 175320 keys from 2001010100 through 2020123123.
contract.hourlyNormalBridge: reviewed 1991-2020 NASA POWER daily T2M normal + (2001-2020 NASA POWER hourly T2M normal - 2001-2020 NASA POWER daily T2M normal)
contract.offset24Convention: 24 UTC is the following UTC midnight and is assigned to the preceding labeled target day.
contract.control: Existing reviewed QORE basket weights (not official EIA gas weights), equal-weighted across 06/12/18/24 UTC.
contract.challengerLocationPrior: Preregistered 2019 EIA-930 marginal gas-dispatch mass: each BA demand exposure times a positive demand-to-gas residual beta, allocated through frozen subregion-to-location mappings; 2020 recalculation is diagnostic only.
contract.locationToEiaRegionRole: Descriptive only; the physical target is restricted directly to the frozen marginal-dispatch balancing-authority universe.
contract.eiaCoverageRule: Each retained target day has at least 23 valid UTC ending hours separately for every selected balancing authority; those same ten BA gas-generation series are summed and divided by 24 to form aggregate average MW.
contract.topDecileHitRate: Recall of the ceil(10% * retained days) highest realized aggregate gas-generation days among the same number of highest model-predicted days; ties use original date order.
limitations: EIA-930 is preliminary operational data, may be revised in place, and does not have final EIA-923 fuel-accounting coverage.
The 2019 fit is physical calibration, not a return optimization; locked 2020 physical validation is now consumed and no longer genuinely unseen.

The full profile is a low-dimensional separable eight-feature design with frozen location weights, four learned UTC offsets, two cooling segments, and fixed ridge regularization; it is not execution-eligible.

marginalDispatchLocationPrior.method: For each BA, residualize adjusted demand and adjusted gas generation within month x local-hour x weekend strata, fit beta=sum(demandResidual*gasResidual)/sum(demandResidual^2), multiply by June-September demand MWh, allocate by frozen subregion demand shares (or declared sole-proxy mapping), and normalize location mass to 1.06.
weaknesses: The demand-to-gas beta is a physical association, not a causal estimate.
Combined MISO subregions 0027 and 0035 require frozen 50/50 location splits.
Balancing-authority boundaries and pseudo-ties are imperfect proxies for local dispatch.
SWPP marginal-dispatch beta is materially less stable in 2020 than the other reviewed BAs.
